newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ CPI falls in Q1 for first time since 1991.
newsitem.headline: NZ CPI falls in Q1 for first time since 1991.

text.p: The New Zealand Consumer Price Index fell by 0.3 percent in the March 1997 quarter, the first fall in the index since the December 1991 quarter, when it fell by 0.1 percent, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Tuesday.

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand had picked 0.1 percent headline inflation in the quarter for an annual 2.2 percent rise, while economists had expected on average a 0.11 percent quarterly rise (2.19 percent annual).
The 0.3 percent fall followed rises of 0.7 percent in the December quarter and 0.6 percent in the September 1996 quarter.

SNZ said credit services contributed the most to the fall, recording a decrease of 5.4 percent, mainly due to a fall in mortgage interest rates. In the credit services group, hire purchase on motor vehicles was the only item to record an increase.
Mortgage interest fell 6.4 percent in the quarter, following a fall of 0.1 percent in the previous quarter.
Food prices had the most significant rise, up 0.7 percent in the quarter.
